hints.title: Player Score Accumulation across Matches
hints.text: A player earns points whether participating as the first player or second player in a match.

hints.title: Score Union Stack with Group Ranking
hints.text: Vertically stack first and second player match scores using union all. Rank players within each group ordered by points descending and player identifier ascending.

hints.title: Tournament Winner Blueprint
hints.text: with TotalScores as (select player_id, sum(score) as score from (select first_player as player_id, first_score as score from Matches union all select second_player as player_id, second_score as score from Matches) s group by player_id), Ranked as (select p.group_id, p.player_id, row_number() over (partition by p.group_id order by coalesce(t.score, 0) desc, p.player_id asc) as rn from Players p left join TotalScores t on p.player_id = t.player_id) select group_id, player_id from Ranked where rn = 1.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
WITH TotalScores AS (
    SELECT player_id, SUM(score) AS score
    FROM (
        SELECT first_player AS player_id, first_score AS score FROM Matches
        UNION ALL
        SELECT second_player AS player_id, second_score AS score FROM Matches
    ) s
    GROUP BY player_id
),
Ranked AS (
    SELECT p.group_id, p.player_id,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
               PARTITION BY p.group_id
               ORDER BY COALESCE(t.score, 0) DESC, p.player_id ASC
           ) AS rn
    FROM Players p
    LEFT JOIN TotalScores t ON p.player_id = t.player_id
)
SELECT group_id, player_id
FROM Ranked
WHERE rn = 1;
```

complexity.notes: Stacking match scores and computing partitioned row ranking executes in linear-logarithmic time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Evaluating only first player scores misses points earned by the same athlete when competing as guest.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Union all unrolls dual match roles into a unified scoring stream prior to window ranking.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Use of UNION ALL to combine host and guest roles, and ROW_NUMBER() with player_id tie breaker.

import pandas as pd

def tournament_winners(players: pd.DataFrame, matches: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    m1 = matches[['first_player', 'first_score']].rename(columns={'first_player': 'player_id', 'first_score': 'score'})
    m2 = matches[['second_player', 'second_score']].rename(columns={'second_player': 'player_id', 'second_score': 'score'})
    scores = pd.concat([m1, m2]).groupby('player_id')['score'].sum().reset_index()
    merged = players.merge(scores, on='player_id', how='left')
    merged['score'] = merged['score'].fillna(0)
    sorted_df = merged.sort_values(by=['group_id', 'score', 'player_id'], ascending=[True, False, True])
    res = sorted_df.drop_duplicates(subset=['group_id'], keep='first')
    return res[['group_id', 'player_id']]
solutions.approach: Pandas Concat Scores and Group Partition Sort
